claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its FCC subsets are caused by variations in short-range order.
Mechanical-property differences among the alloys are caused by local compositional fluctuations.
The quinary alloy and the relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
The controlled comparison reduces constituent count from five to four and three while retaining equiatomic compositions and single-phase FCC structures.
The alloys are to be compared by room-temperature tensile deformation at identical strain rates and environmental conditions.
Short-range order and local compositional fluctuations constitute the structural mediators between constituent count and mechanical response.
Variations in short-range order and compositional fluctuations alter the local energy landscape.
The altered local energy landscape changes dislocation pinning.
The altered local energy landscape changes dislocation cross-slip.
Variations in short-range order and compositional fluctuations affect activation of deformation twinning or stacking-fault formation.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have greater short-range order and compositional fluctuations than the quinary alloy.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have higher yield strength than the quinary alloy.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have lower ductility than the quinary alloy.
Increased short-range order and compositional fluctuations raise strength by hindering dislocation motion.
Increased short-range order and compositional fluctuations reduce ductility by promoting localized deformation mechanisms.
The comparison is applicable only when all alloys remain single-phase FCC and receive identical thermomechanical conditions.
X-ray diffraction or atom-probe tomography can be used to quantify the proposed short-range-order and compositional-fluctuation mediators.
The hypothesis is falsified if the subsets do not show both the predicted mechanical-property changes or if the proposed mediators are not significantly different among the alloys.
